name: Flat lay composition
summary: A still life of objects on a flat surface, shot from straight above.
how: Hold the camera at 90° above the surface.
Group 5 to 9 objects and keep 30% to 40% of the frame empty.
Align objects at 0° and 90°, and repeat one accent colour in 3 props.
Light the set from a window at the side.

origin.note: Andrew Kromelow, a worker at Frank Gehry's studio, names the habit of laying objects at right angles knolling in 1987.

adoptions.via: Instagram users post overhead photos of coffee, notebooks and flowers on pale surfaces.
